senses.gloss: A painful ordeal made up of one attack or test after another.
examples: Every nominee has to run the *gauntlet* of Senate hearings.
Reporters formed a *gauntlet* the mayor had to walk through.
Getting the permit meant a *gauntlet* of city offices and forms.

senses.gloss: One model or version in a series of products, each replacing the one before it.
examples: The new *generation* of electric trucks goes twice as far.
This phone is two *generations* behind mine.
The camera is in its fourth *generation* now.

senses.gloss: The producing of something such as electricity, heat, or income.
examples: Wind now accounts for a third of the state's power *generation*.
The plant's *generation* dropped during the heat wave.
Their whole marketing budget goes to lead *generation*.

senses.gloss: The physical features and layout of a particular place.
examples: The *geography* of the valley makes flooding worse every spring.
A river on one side and cliffs on the other give the town an awkward *geography*.
The troops studied the *geography* of the coast before landing.

senses.gloss: The shape of an object and the way its parts are arranged.
examples: Engineers changed the *geometry* of the wing to cut drag.
The bike's *geometry* makes it steady on fast descents.
Every snowflake grows in a six-sided *geometry*.

senses.gloss: The long period in which an idea or project develops before it appears.
examples: The film had a ten-year *gestation* before it reached theaters.
After a long *gestation*, the bill finally came to a vote.
The album is still in *gestation*.

senses.gloss: A woman's close female friend.
examples: She's out to dinner with her *girlfriends*.
My mom takes a trip with three *girlfriends* every fall.
I called my oldest *girlfriend* the minute I heard the news.

senses.gloss: Something that accidentally reveals a secret or the truth.
examples: The paint under his fingernails was a dead *giveaway*.
Her smile was the *giveaway* that she already knew.
The misspelled address is a *giveaway* that the email is fake.

senses.gloss: The head of a Mafia family or other crime organization.
examples: Prosecutors named him as the *godfather* of the city's crime family.
Two *godfathers* met to divide up the territory.
Agents spent years building a case against the *godfather*.

senses.gloss: A man seen as the founder or leading early figure of a movement or style.
examples: He's often called the *godfather* of hip-hop.
Those two are the *godfathers* of modern stand-up.
She thanked the *godfather* of the genre in her acceptance speech.

senses.gloss: A friendly, helpful feeling toward other people.
examples: The apology was meant as a gesture of *goodwill*.
Years of *goodwill* between the two towns ended over the water dispute.
He built up a lot of *goodwill* helping neighbors shovel snow.

senses.gloss: A device that keeps an engine from running faster than a set speed.
examples: The delivery vans have a *governor* set at 65.
Somebody had taken the *governor* off the go-kart.
A broken *governor* let the engine race until it seized.

senses.gloss: A member of a board that runs an institution such as a central bank.
examples: The Fed *governor* voted against the rate cut.
The board of *governors* meets again in March.
Two *governors* dissented from the decision.

senses.gloss: The steepness of a slope, or the rate at which something rises or falls.
examples: The road climbs at a steep *gradient* for two miles.
Engineers eased the *gradient* so loaded trucks could make the hill.
There's a sharp temperature *gradient* between the coast and the desert.

senses.gloss: A place where old, broken, or unwanted things are left to sit.
senses.ru: свалка, кладбище (старой техники и т. п.)
examples: The desert base is a *graveyard* for retired airliners.
That drawer is a *graveyard* of dead batteries and old cables.
The late time slot became a *graveyard* for new shows.

senses.gloss: A situation in which nothing gets decided because opposing sides block each other.
examples: Budget *gridlock* shut the government down for weeks.
Voters say they're tired of *gridlock* in Congress.
The two departments have been in *gridlock* since spring.

senses.gloss: A person or group that protects or defends something.
examples: The courts see themselves as *guardians* of the Constitution.
She became the *guardian* of her grandfather's letters and photographs.
Editors are supposed to be *guardians* of accuracy.

senses.gloss: A rule or limit put in place to keep something from going badly wrong.
examples: The law puts *guardrails* on how the data can be used.
Every trading desk needs *guardrails*.
Without some kind of *guardrail*, the costs will get away from us.

senses.gloss: A small separate house on someone's property where guests stay.
examples: My in-laws stay in the *guesthouse* when they visit.
The listing includes a two-bedroom *guesthouse* out back.
They turned the *guesthouse* into an office during the pandemic.

senses.gloss: A made-up fact that an AI system states as if it were true.
examples: The case he cited turned out to be a *hallucination*.
Two lawyers were fined for filing a brief full of *hallucinations*.
Newer models reduce *hallucination* but don't eliminate it.

senses.gloss: Ground beef sold raw by weight and cooked loose rather than as a patty.
examples: Pick up a pound of *hamburger* for the chili.
Brown the *hamburger* before you add the sauce.
*Hamburger* was on sale, so I bought two packages.

senses.gloss: A game in which players hit a small rubber ball against a wall with their hands.
examples: They play *handball* at the courts in the park every Saturday.
He grew up hitting a ball against a schoolyard wall, playing *handball* for hours.
A hard *handball* game will tear up your palms.

senses.gloss: In soccer, the foul of touching the ball with the hand or arm.
examples: The referee called a *handball* in the box.
That *handball* cost them a penalty kick.
The replay showed it wasn't a *handball* at all.

senses.gloss: The way a vehicle responds to steering and to the road.
examples: The new suspension improved the car's *handling*.
Reviewers praised its *handling* on wet pavement.
Oversized tires hurt the *handling* a little.

senses.gloss: Something left over from an earlier time that no longer fits.
examples: The rule is a *hangover* from the 1970s.
That fee is a *hangover* from the old contract.
Downtown is still working through the *hangover* of the building boom.

senses.gloss: Baseball played with a regulation hard ball, as opposed to softball.
examples: He played *hardball* all four years of high school.
The league moves kids from tee-ball to *hardball* at age nine.
Our office team plays softball, not *hardball*.

senses.gloss: The physical parts of a computer or electronic system, as opposed to the programs.
examples: The software is fine; the problem is the *hardware*.
Training a model that size takes expensive *hardware*.
Our *hardware* is five years old and it shows.

senses.gloss: Heavy weapons and military equipment.
examples: The convoy carried millions of dollars of military *hardware*.
Both sides moved *hardware* toward the border.
The parade showed off the country's newest *hardware*.

senses.gloss: Something that causes a lot of trouble or annoyance.
examples: The new billing system has been a *headache* from day one.
Parking downtown is a real *headache*.
Merging the two databases created *headaches* nobody predicted.
